source.title: On the Limitations of Steering in Language Model Alignment
source.authors: Chebrolu Niranjan; Kokil Jaidka; G. Yeo

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the original refusal-direction study but does not test or rely on that refusal finding. Its experiments concern value steering for demographic bias, not refusal behavior or the difference-in-means refusal direction.
record.gate_note: No refusal-related direction is measured, removed, added, or tested, and no refusal behavior is evaluated. The reported GPT-2 XL examples apply steering to demographic/value prompts and are recorded under fits_no_version. The listed layers and coefficients are steering settings, not outcome results. The antonym-task causal analysis is used to select intervention layers, not reported as a result about refusal.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Arditi et al. (2024) only as an example of steering-vector use. Its experiments add antonym-based value vectors to GPT-2 XL on demographic-bias prompts. It never constructs a harmful-minus-harmless direction, never ablates or adds a refusal direction, and never measures refusal, so its results bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. Steering shows promise for bias mitigation and value alignment, but struggles with consistency in complex social contexts and can introduce factual errors through overcorrection.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses antonym-based value vectors added at selected layers of GPT-2 XL for demographic/value steering. It does not construct or ablate the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, nor test refusal behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different steering targets and empirically tuned layer/coefficient settings; its qualitative examples show varying outcomes across social scenarios.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 XL, adding Equality and Impartial vectors shifted one hiring completion from religious favoritism to a merit-based choice.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Antonym-based value steering can reduce explicit demographic bias in simple prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: In a legal prompt, steering produced a factually distorted denial of involvement, which the authors call overcorrection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Value steering can introduce factual distortion in socially sensitive scenarios.

fits_no_version.finding: In an election prompt, the steered output contained contradictory details.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Value steering can be inconsistent in complex social contexts.

record.problems: The reported steering outcomes are qualitative examples rather than quantitative evaluations. The paper tests only GPT-2 XL and does not measure refusal or preservation of general capabilities.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant refusal-direction results were reported. The antonym-task causal analysis and layer-selection results were not included because they select intervention points rather than test the claim.

untested.parts: Untested: the refusal direction, its ablation or addition, refusal rates, and capability preservation.
Untested: jailbreak suppression of the direction and adversarial training against its ablation.
Untested: multi-direction or cone structure of refusal.
Untested: separation of harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
Untested: transfer across languages, model variants, or base to instruct.
Untested: the role of how and when refusal is trained.
Untested: reasoning models (mentioned only as future work).

record.verdict_notes: This is a short proof-of-concept preprint built on one qualitative example per scenario in GPT-2 XL. It reports no quantitative results and no refusal measures. The CIE antonym analysis is used only to select intervention layers. The reader's T6/cites_only call is confirmed.

versions.untested_parts: The harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, its removal or addition, refusal rates, and preservation of other abilities are not tested.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is evaluated.
No jailbreak suppression of the refusal direction or training against its ablation is evaluated.
The paper does not test whether refusal is represented by one direction, an affine structure, a cone, or multiple directions.
No distinction between harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions is tested.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer of a refusal direction is tested.
No refusal training method or training stage is varied.
No reasoning model or reasoning-before-answer behavior is tested.

rows.subject: GPT-2 XL
rows.operation_detail: Added value-steering vectors at selected layers

conditions.value: Recruiter choosing between Sean Morgan and Maria Antonella Estupinan

rows.measure: Qualitative output regarding hiring decision and bias
rows.baseline: Unsteered output favored the Christian candidate and referred to the importance of church.
rows.value: Steered output selected the woman, stating she was the best candidate for the job.
rows.note: Qualitative example of value steering, not a refusal test.
rows.check: This is a value-steering bias example, not refusal. The reader's 'observed' state has no referent for any version, so it is set to cannot_determine.

rows.subject: GPT-2 XL
rows.operation_detail: Added value-steering vectors at selected layers
rows.measure: Qualitative output regarding the case and factual accuracy
rows.baseline: Unsteered output described Hassan as a threat and referred to evidence of violent incidents.
rows.value: Steered output said he was not a party to the lawsuit and had no knowledge of it; the authors describe this as overcorrection and factual distortion.
rows.note: Qualitative example of value steering, not a refusal test.
rows.check: This is a value-steering legal-scenario example, not refusal. It is a single qualitative output, and no version applies.

rows.subject: GPT-2 XL
rows.operation_detail: Added value-steering vectors at selected layers

conditions.value: Student senate election involving Kwame Matthews and Lucy Fen Xiu

rows.measure: Qualitative output consistency in the election scenario
rows.baseline: Unsteered output said Fen Xiu was elected and included her acceptance speech.
rows.value: Steered output introduced contradictory details about the candidates and election; the authors describe difficulty maintaining consistency in this complex context.
rows.note: Qualitative example of value steering, not a refusal test.
rows.check: This is a value-steering election example, not refusal. It is a single qualitative output, and no version applies.
